title: Sally Hilton — 2nd Substantive Review decision summary (2026-07-01)
text:
BEFORE THE FITNESS TO PRACTISE COMMITTEE
OF THE GENERAL OPTICAL COUNCIL

GENERAL OPTICAL COUNCIL

F(24)03

AND

SALLY HILTON (D-11927)

PRIVATE HEARING
___________________________________________________________________

DETERMINATION OF A SUBSTANTIVE REVIEW
01 July 2026

Committee Members:
Clive Powell (Chair/Lay)

Ann McKechin (Lay)

Miriam Karp (Lay)

Ian Taylor (Dispensing Optician)

Sarah Baylay (Dispensing Optician)

Legal adviser: Jeff Widdup

Clinical Adviser: Jennifer Bearn

GOC Presenting Officer: Leonie Hinds

Registrant: Not present and represented

Registrant representative: Dean Smith

Hearings Officer: Arjeta Shabani

Outcome: Impairment found – Indefinite Suspension

___________________________________________________________________

DETERMINATION
Background
1. The substantive hearing took place on 23 - 24 May 2024, 28 – 31 May 2024 and
29 July 2024. The substantive Fitness to Practise Committee found the allegation
proved pursuant to Rule 46 (12) of the General Optical Council (Fitness to Practise)
Rules Order of Council 2013 (the Rules).

Second Substantive Review Hearing - 01 July 2026

Preliminary matters
2. Ms Hinds applied for the entirety of the hearing to be dealt with in private. The
Committee heard and accepted the advice of the Legal Adviser with respect to the
application.
3. The Committee was satisfied that it was appropriate for all of the hearing to be
heard in private.

Findings on Impairment
4. The Committee found that the Registrant’s fitness to practise as a Dispensing
Optician is currently impaired.

Sanction
5. Having determined that the Registrant’s fitness to practise is currently impaired,
the Committee went on to consider an appropriate sanction.
6. The Committee determined that the proportionate order would be an order of
indefinite suspension which would come into effect at the end of the current order
of suspension.

Chairman of the Committee: Clive Powell

Signature
Date: 01 July 2026

FURTHER INFORMATION
Transcript
A full transcript of the hearing will be made available for purchase in due course.
Appeal
Any appeal against an order of the Committee must be lodged with the relevant court within
28 days of the service of this notification. If no appeal is lodged, the order will take effect at
the end of that period. The relevant court is shown at section 23G(4)(a)-(c) of the Opticians
Act 1989 (as amended).
Professional Standards Authority
This decision will be reported to the Professional Standards Authority (PSA) under the
provisions of section 29 of the NHS Reform and Healthcare Professions Act 2002. PSA may
refer this case to the High Court of Justice in England and Wales, the Court of Session in
Scotland or the High Court of Justice in Northern Ireland as appropriate if they decide that a
decision has been insufficient to protect the public and/or should not have been made, and
if they consider that referral is desirable for the protection of the public.
Where a registrant can appeal against a decision, the Authority has 40 days beginning with
the day which is the last day in which you can appeal. Where a registrant cannot appeal
against the outcome of a hearing, the Authority’s appeal period is 56 days beginning with
the day in which notification of the decision was served on you. PSA will notify you promptly
of a decision to refer. A letter will be sent by recorded delivery to your registered address
(unless PSA has been notified by the GOC of a change of address).

Effect of orders for suspension or erasure
To practise or carry on business as an optometrist or dispensing optician, to take or use a
description which implies registration or entitlement to undertake any activity which the law
restricts to a registered person, may amount to a criminal offence once an entry in the
register has been suspended or erased.
